en: Śrīṃ! Homage to Mañjunātha.
Then the glorious Vajradhara, the supreme tamer, the hero who conquers the three worlds, the Lord of Secrets, the Master of the Vajra, [spoke]. (1)
His eyes were like blossomed white lotuses and his face was like a fully opened lotus;
he repeatedly caressed the excellent flute with his own hand.
Led by Bhṛkuṭītaraṅga and others, there were Vajrapāṇis who were unassailable, heroic subduers of the wicked, and who consumed the flesh of heroes with a sense of awe-inspiring loathsomeness. || 3 ||
With their own hands brandishing millions of flashing vajras,
they are supreme, holding the medicine of wisdom, skillful means, and great compassion.

Together with nāgas whose dispositions were joyful and contented, who were delighted, who had swallowed up anger and strife, who performed the deeds of a Buddha, and who possessed bodies capable of leaping into the abyss; || 5 ||
Having prostrated before the Lord, the Fully Awakened One, the Blessed One, the Tathāgata,
he stood before him with palms joined in reverence and spoke these words.
For my greatness, for my sake, and out of compassion for me, O All-Pervading Lord, [grant that] I may become an attainer of the perfect awakening through the Net of Illusion. (7)
The Chanting of the Names of Mañjuśrī (Nāmasaṃgīti)
For the benefit of all sentient beings who are mired in the mud of ignorance and whose minds are agitated by the afflictions, and for the attainment of the unsurpassed fruit. (8)
May the Perfectly Awakened One, the Blessed One, the Teacher, the Guru of the World—knower of the reality of the great samaya, supreme knower of the faculties and inclinations—reveal [it]. (3)
O Blessed One, [I bow] to the one whose body is gnosis, the Great Uṣṇīṣa, the Lord of Speech, Mañjuśrī the Knowledge-Being, the embodiment of gnosis, the Self-Arisen One. (10)
The supreme Nāmasaṃgīti, which possesses profound meaning, is sublime, of great significance, peerless, auspicious, and virtuous in its beginning, middle, and end. (11)
It has been spoken by the Buddhas of the past, it will be spoken by those of the future, and the perfectly awakened ones of the present speak it again and again. (13)
And that which is being chanted here in the great Māyājāla,
by the joyful and immeasurable holders of mantras who bear the great thunderbolt.
And I shall maintain this with a firm resolve until final liberation, just as you, O Lord, the holder of the secrets of all the Buddhas. (14)
I shall reveal [this] for the sake of sentient beings according to the distinctions of their inclinations, in order to destroy all afflictions and to eliminate the remainder of ignorance. (15)
Having thus entreated the Tathāgata, Guhyendra Vajrapāṇi stood before him with his palms joined in reverence. (16)
There are sixteen [verses] of the *adhyeṣaṇā-gāthā*.
Śākyamuni, the perfectly awakened one, the supreme among bipeds,
extended his long, broad, and beautiful tongue from his own mouth.
Displaying a smile that purifies the three lower realms for all beings, which illuminates the three worlds and subdues the four Māras; || 2 ||
The Chanting of the Names of Mañjuśrī (Nāmasaṃgīti)
Filling the three worlds with her sweet and divine voice,
she addressed the Lord of Secrets, the mighty Vajrapāṇi.
Excellent, O glorious Vajradhara! Excellent to you, O Vajrapāṇi, you who, endowed with great compassion, act for the sake of the welfare of the world. (4)
You are prepared to hear from me the *Nāmasaṃgīti*, which possesses great significance, is purifying, and destroys all sins—the [mantra] of Mañjuśrī’s wisdom-body. (5)
"Therefore, O Lord, please teach this well; I am your humble servant.
"Listen with a one-pointed mind," [he replied]. "Very well, Blessed One," [the other said]. (6)
Six verses of response.
Then the Blessed One Śākyamuni, having surveyed the entire great family of mantras, the family of mantra-vidyādharas, and the three families, [spoke]. (1)
The worldly and supramundane family, the great family that illuminates the world, the supreme Mahāmudrā family, and the great Mahoṣṇīṣa family. (2)
The Two Verses on the Sixfold Vision.
The Lord of Speech uttered this verse, which is of great majesty and joined with six royal mantras, concerning those whose nature is the non-arising of phenomena.
Śrā ī u ū e ai śrī śrī śraṃ śraḥ, abiding in the heart;
the embodiment of wisdom, the Buddha among the Buddhas who exist throughout the three times. || 2 ||
Oṃ! Homage to you, Vajratīkṣṇa, whose form is the wisdom-knowledge that cuts through suffering; to you, the Lord of Speech, who composes the words of the knowledge-body. || 3 ||
Three Verses on the Sequence of Awakening through the Net of Illusion (Māyājālābhisaṃbodhikramagāthā)
The Chanting of the Names (Nāmasaṃgīti)
Thus the Blessed One, the Buddha, the Perfectly Awakened One, is born from the syllable *A*; he is the syllable *Ka*, worthy of all offerings, of great significance, and the Supreme Mother. (1)
The Great Vital Breath is non-arising and devoid of verbal expression; it is beyond all causes of linguistic designation and is the supreme radiance of all speech. (2)
The Great Festival of great passion, who brings joy to all sentient beings;
the Great Festival of great hatred, the great enemy of all afflictions. || 3 ||
He is the great festival of the great delusion, the crusher of the delusion of the dull-witted;
he is the great festival of the great wrath, the great enemy of great anger.
The great festival, the great greed, the destroyer of all greed;
the great desire, the great fame, the great delusion, the great delight. || 5 ||
He has great marshlands, a great body, a great complexion, and a great form;
he has a great name, is most noble, and possesses a vast and extensive mandala.
He who wields the great weapon of wisdom, the supreme leader with the great goad for the afflictions;
he of great renown, great fame, great light, and great radiance.
The wise one who possesses the Great Illusion, the accomplisher of the purpose of the Great Illusion, he who delights in the Great Illusion, and the great illusory Indra-bamboo flute. || 8 ||
The most excellent great lord of donors, the foremost upholder of great morality, the steadfast possessor of great patience, and one of great vigor and prowess. || 3 ||
Abiding in the samādhi of great meditative concentration, possessing the body of great wisdom,
he is of great power, possesses great skillful means, and is an ocean of the knowledge of his vows.
He is composed of great love, the object of measure, the Great Compassionate One of supreme intellect;
he is of great wisdom, of great intelligence, of great means, and of great form. || 11 ||
Endowed with great wisdom, possessing great speed, a great boatman;
possessed of great supernatural power, a great lord, and of great strength and prowess. || 12 ||
The Chanting of the Names of Mañjuśrī (Nāmasaṃgīti)
The shatterer of the great mountain of existence, the dense wielder of the great vajra;
the greatly fierce, the greatly terrible, the one who causes fear even to the fearful. || 13 ||
The Lord is the supreme among great vidyās, the Guru is the supreme among great mantras;
he is one who has mounted the way of the Mahāyāna and is the highest within the Mahāyāna system. || 14 ||
Mahāvairocana is the Buddha, the great observer of silence, the great sage;
he is born from the Great Way of Mantra and has the Great Way of Mantra as his very essence. || 1 ||
He has attained the ten perfections; he is the locus of the ten perfections;
he is the purity of the ten perfections; he is the method of the ten perfections. || 2 ||
The Lord is the master of the ten stages, established upon the ten stages;
his self is purified by the ten knowledges, and he maintains the purity of the ten knowledges. (3)
The Lord of Sages possesses ten aspects, is the goal of the ten goals, and is the all-pervading one endowed with the ten powers;
he effects the welfare of the entire world remaining and has mastery over the ten forms.
He whose self is free from the proliferation of phenomena such as clouds, whose self is pure, whose self is suchness;
he who speaks what is real, who speaks according to reality, who acts according to his words, and whose speech is never otherwise.
He speaks what is beneficial and non-deceptive, abides at the limit of reality, roars the lion’s roar of selflessness, and terrifies the deer-like followers of false paths. (6)
All-pervading, with unfailing course, possessing the speed of a Tathāgata’s mind; the Victor who has conquered his enemies, the triumphant one, a universal monarch of great power. || 7 ||

He is the leader of the hosts, the teacher of the hosts, the lord of the hosts, the master of the hosts, self-controlled, of great majesty, preeminent, not led by others, and possessed of the great path. || 8 ||
Lord of speech, master of words, eloquent, lord of eloquence, whose song is infinite, truthful in speech, speaker of truth, and teacher of the Four Truths. || 3 ||
The Chanting of the Names of Mañjuśrī.
For he is the non-retrogressive one, the non-returner, the rhinoceros-like solitary leader;
he has emerged through various means of deliverance and is the single cause of the great elements. || 10 ||
The Arhat, the monk whose outflows are exhausted, free from passion, with senses conquered,
has attained security, attained fearlessness, become cooled, and is undisturbed. || 11 ||
Endowed with perfect wisdom and conduct, the Sugata, the supreme knower of the world, free from possessiveness and egoism, stands firm in the method of truth and compassion. || 12 ||

Standing at the far shore of saṃsāra, having accomplished what was to be done, he stands on firm ground through his steadfastness in the knowledge of absolute liberation; armed with the weapon of wisdom, he is the destroyer [of ignorance]. || 13 ||
He is the True Dharma, the King of Dharma, the radiant one, the supreme illuminator of the world;
he is the Dharma-king within the Dharma and the instructor of the path. || 14 ||
He whose purpose is accomplished, whose resolve is fulfilled, who is free from all conceptual constructions, the non-conceptual, inexhaustible realm—the supreme, imperishable dharmadhātu. || 15 ||

He is the meritorious one, the accumulation of merit, knowledge, the great mine of knowledge, the possessor of knowledge, the knower of the existent and non-existent, and he who is endowed with the two accumulations. || 16 ||

He is eternal, the sovereign of the universe, the yogi, meditation itself, the object of meditation, and the lord of the intellects; he is indeed to be realized within one's own self, immovable, the supreme goal, and the sustainer of the three bodies.
The Buddha consists of the five bodies; the all-pervading Lord consists of the five gnoses; he has the five Buddhas as his crown and possesses the five unimpeded eyes. || 18 ||
The progenitor of all Buddhas, the supreme and most excellent son of the Buddha, born from the source of wisdom, the womb of the Dharma, he who brings an end to existence. (13)
The Self is the singular mass of light, the newborn Lord of the universe, born from the sky, self-existent, the great fire of wisdom and knowledge. ||20||
The Chanting of the Names.
Vairocana, the great radiance, the light of the splendor of gnosis; the lamp of the world, the fire of gnosis, possessed of great majesty, and self-luminous. || 21 ||

This King of Vidyās is the Lord here, the King of Purity who accomplishes the great purpose; he is the Uṣṇīṣa born from the Great Uṣṇīṣa, the beholder of the universe, and the master of calamities. || 33 ||
The venerable embodiment of all Buddhas, whose eyes bring joy to the world, the creator of the universal form, the pure one, the worthy of honor, the great seer. || 33 ||

The mantra-practitioner upholds the three families, maintains the mantra of the great samaya, bears the Three Jewels, is most excellent, and is the supreme teacher of the Vehicle of the Women (Striyāna). || 24 ||
The conqueror with the noose of delusion, the wielder of the vajra-noose, the great planet;
he who has the thunderbolt as his goad, the great noose, and who is terrifying with the form of the thunderbolt-bhairava. || 25 ||
Twenty-five verses on the wisdom of the perfectly pure realm of phenomena (suviśuddhadharmadhātujñāna).
The King of Wrath, six-faced and formidable, with six eyes and six forms, powerful, a skeleton terrifying with fangs, possessing hundreds of faces like the Halāhala poison. || 1 ||
Yamātaka, Vighnarāj, Vajravega, Bhayaṃkara, Vighuṣṭavajra, Hṛdvajra, Māyāvajrī, and Mahodara. || 2 ||
The Lord of the Thunderbolt, whose source is the Vajra, whose mandala is like the sky, who wears a single matted lock that quivers, and who is clothed in an elephant hide. || 3 ||
The cry of "Hā hā" is most terrible; the cry of "Hī hī" is fearsome; the "Śraṭṭā" laugh is a great roar; the "Vajra" laugh is a mighty sound. || 4 ||
Vajrasattva, the Great Being; Vajrarātra, the Great Bliss; Vajracaṇḍa, the Great Joy; Vajrabhṛkuṭī, the Utterer of Hūṃ. || 5 ||
Wielding the vajra as armor and weapon, he is the vajra-sword that cuts through all; the wielder of the universal thunderbolt, the peerless hero who destroys all afflictions.
The Chanting of the Names of Mañjuśrī (Nāmasaṃgīti)
His eyes are formidable with vajra-flames; his hair is vajra-flames;
he is the vajra-penetration, the great penetration; he has a hundred eyes and vajra-eyes. || 7 ||
His claws are like the tips of forest trees, and his skin is as dense and firm as the essence of a diamond.
Wearing a garland of thunderbolts, glorious, adorned with ornaments of thunderbolts, possessing the sound of "hā hā" and loud laughter, the resonance of the thunderbolt, he is supreme. || 3 ||
Mañjughoṣa, the great roar, the sole sound of the three worlds, the great one whose voice extends to the limits of the realm of space, the best among those who possess a voice. || 10 ||
Ten Verses in Praise of Mirror-like Wisdom (Ādarśajñāna)
Suchness, true selflessness, the limit of reality, the immediate, the proclaimer of emptiness, the bull among men, who roars with a deep and sublime voice. || 1 ||
He is the great-sounding conch of Dharma, the great drum of Dharma, the unestablished Nirvana, and the celestial drum of Dharma resounding in the ten directions. ||2||
The glory of the manifestation of all forms, which brings about the reflection of everything without exception.
Invincible, renowned as the Great Lord, the sovereign of the triple world; established upon the exalted Noble Path, the banner of Dharma, he is of great majesty. || 4 ||

He whose body is the unique youth of the three worlds, the ancient and venerable Lord of Creatures, who bears the thirty-two marks of excellence, the beloved one, beautiful throughout the three worlds. || 5 ||

The teacher of the qualities of worldly knowledge, the teacher of the world, the fearless one, the protector, the savior, the friend of the three worlds, the refuge, the deliverer, the unsurpassed. || 6 ||
He enjoys the vast expanse of the sky, an ocean of the wisdom of omniscience; he is the shatterer of the shell of the egg of ignorance and the destroyer of the cage of existence. || 7 ||
The Chanting of the Names of Mañjuśrī (Nāmasaṃgīti)
Having pacified all afflictions, having reached the further shore of the ocean of saṃsāra, crowned with the consecration of primordial wisdom, and adorned as a perfectly awakened Buddha. || 8 ||

He who is the three-fold destroyer of suffering, the pacifier of pain, the one beyond the three [realms], the infinite, the one who has attained the threefold liberation, who is freed from all obscurations, and who has reached equality with space. ||3||
He has transcended all stains of affliction and attained mastery over the three times;
he is the great elephant among all sentient beings, the crest-jewel upon the crest of all virtues. 10.

Completely liberated from all substrates, well-established on the path of space, the all-pervading Lord is the bearer of the great wish-fulfilling gem of the mind, the supreme among all jewels. || 11 ||

He is a vast and flourishing great wish-fulfilling tree, a magnificent and supreme jar of fortune; he is the performer of deeds that benefit all sentient beings, a well-wisher, and one who is affectionate toward the virtuous. || 13 ||
He knows the auspicious and the inauspicious; he knows the [proper] time, he knows the right occasion, and he is all-pervading and sovereign.
He knows the faculties of beings, he knows the [right] moment, and he is skilled in the three liberations. (13)

He is possessed of virtues, a knower of virtues, a knower of dharma, praised, the source of auspiciousness, the most auspicious of all auspicious things, and the embodiment of fame, fortune, glory, and well-being. || 14 ||
He is the great festival, the great relief, the great bliss, and the great delight; he is honor, hospitality, prosperity, joy, fortune, and the lord of glory. || 15 ||
He is the most excellent, the giver of boons, the supreme, the worthy refuge, the best of shelters,
the enemy of great fear, the most eminent, and the destroyer of every last trace of fear.

He who has a crest, who wears a peacock feather, who is a student, who is a young maiden, who is shaven-headed, who wears a crown, who is five-faced, who has five tufts of hair, who is the thief of the five senses, and whose head is adorned with locks. || 17 ||
Wearing the great vows, girded with the sacred grass-cord, a celibate student, the best of those who observe vows,
a great ascetic devoted to austerity, a graduate of the Vedic studies, Gautama was the foremost leader.
The knower of Brahman is the Brāhmaṇa; he has attained the nirvāṇa of Brahman.
He is liberation, emancipation, the limb of liberation, freedom, the state of Śakti, and Śiva. (13)
Nirvāṇa, cessation, peace, the supreme good, liberation, the end of pleasure and pain, the ultimate goal, dispassion, and the exhaustion of the substrata—these are synonyms. (20)
The Chanting of the Names (Nāmasaṃgīti)
He who is incomparable, unmanifest, without appearance, and stainless;
partless, all-pervading, omnipresent, subtle, the seed, and untainted. || 21 ||
He who is heroic, stainless, free from the defects of speech, and without affliction;
he who is perfectly awakened, whose self is enlightened, the omniscient one, and the supreme knower of all. (22)
Transcending the nature of consciousness, he assumes a form of non-dual gnosis;
free from conceptual construction and effortless, he performs the enlightened activities of the three worlds. || 23 ||
The Buddha is without beginning or end, the primordial Buddha (Ādibuddha) who is without parts;
he is the stainless single eye of gnosis, the embodiment of gnosis, the Tathāgata. || 24 ||
Lord of Speech, great debater, king of speakers, bull among disputants; best of those who speak, most excellent, lion of speakers, unconquered. || 25 ||
Samattadaśī, Prāmodya, Uṣṇīṣamālī, Sudarśana, Śrīvatsa, Suprabha, Dīpti, Bhābhāsvaraka, and Raghuṭi. || 26 ||
The supreme and most excellent great physician, the peerless remover of thorns, he who is the tree of all medicinal herbs and the great enemy of the disease of the afflictions. || 27 ||
The beloved Tilaka of the three worlds, the glorious circle of stars,
extending to the sky of the ten directions, he is the great height of the wealth of Dharma.
The sole vast parasol for the world, whose mandala is loving-kindness and compassion;
the glorious Padmārteśvara, the great sovereign Ratnacchattra. || 23 ||
The great king of all Buddhas, who sustains the embodiment of all Buddhas;
the great yoga of all Buddhas, the sole teaching of all Buddhas. || 30 ||
He is the glory of the consecration with the vajra-jewel, the sovereign lord of all jewel-lords, the lord of the lords of all worlds, and the supreme ruler who wields all vajras. || 31 ||
The great mind of all Buddhas, the movement of the minds of all Buddhas, the great body of all Buddhas, and the Sarasvatī of all Buddhas. || 32 ||
The Chanting of the Names of Mañjuśrī (Nāmasaṃgīti)
Vajrasūrya is the great light; Vatreṇḍa is the stainless radiance; Virāgādi is the great passion; Viśvaprabha is the universal light. || 33 ||
He is the lion-throne of the Perfectly Awakened One, the mother of the Dharma through the assembly of Buddhas;
he is the glorious one born from the lotus of the Buddha, the holder of the treasury of omniscient wisdom. (34)
The king who wields the universal illusion, the great master of the Buddhas' vidyā;
the adamantine sharpness, the great sword, utterly pure, and supreme beyond the transcendent. (35)
He who wields the great weapon of the Dharma for the sake of cutting off suffering, whose depth is as unshakeable as a diamond, and whose intellect is like a thunderbolt— Vajrapāṇi, he has arrived.
He is the fulfillment of all perfections, the ornament of all the stages, the selflessness of pure phenomena, and the radiance of the moon of perfect wisdom from his heart. || 37 ||
The great exertion of the Net of Illusion, the supreme sovereign of all tantras,
seated upon the coils of the serpent Śeṣa, he who sustains the entire body of gnosis.
Samantabhadra, the one of excellent intellect, Kṣitigarbha, the protector of the world;
the great womb of all Buddhas, the bearer of the wheel of universal emanations. || 33 ||
The direct realization of all phenomena belongs to the Sage whose intellect has reached the ultimate reality. || 41 ||
Stable, with a perfectly serene self, he holds the right awakening of a *saṃbuddha*;
he is manifest before all Buddhas, a flame of gnosis, most brilliantly radiant. (43)
Forty-two verses on the wisdom of discerning observation.
The supreme accomplisher of desired aims, the purifier from all miserable states, the most excellent protector, the liberator of all sentient beings. (1)
The Chanting of the Names of Mañjuśrī (Nāmasaṃgīti)

The sole hero in the battle against the afflictions, the destroyer of the pride of the enemy that is ignorance; possessing wisdom, he bears the sentiment of the erotic, the illustrious one who manifests the sentiments of the heroic and the loathsome. (2)
The placement of feet in hundreds of such strides is his dance;
the expansive span of his glorious arms is his dance across the expanse of the sky. || 3 ||
Standing upon the surface of the earth with the sole of one foot, he stands with the tip of the nail of his big toe resting upon the summit of the cosmic egg. || 4 ||
The purpose of the Dharma is imperishable in the ultimate sense;
within the single reality, the various representations are to be mastered, for the continuum of mind and consciousness is but a stream.
Delighting in the meaning of all phenomena without exception, delighting in emptiness, possessing profound wisdom,
he has transcended passion for existence and finds great delight in the three realms of existence.
Pure, white as a bright cloud, with the beautiful luster of the autumn moon's rays;
possessing the radiance of the orb of the rising sun, and the glow of great red jewels upon his nails. || 7 ||
With a crown of pure sapphire and bearing the luster of great blue gems, he possesses the splendor of the rays of great jewels and is adorned with the emanations of the Buddhas.
He who causes a hundred world-systems to tremble, whose great stride is the bases of psychic power;
he who possesses great mindfulness, the reality itself, the king of the four foundations of mindfulness and meditative concentration.
He is the ocean of the Tathāgata’s qualities, fragrant with the flowers of the factors of enlightenment;
he knows the method of the eightfold path and perfectly understands the way of the Fully Enlightened One.
He is the great attachment to all beings, yet free from attachment like the sky;
he is known by the minds of all beings, and possesses the speed of the minds of all beings. || 11 ||
He knows the faculties and objects of all sentient beings; he captivates the minds of all sentient beings.
He knows the reality of the meaning of the five aggregates and maintains the purity of the five aggregates. 12.
Abiding at the limit of all emanations, skilled in all emanations;
established on the path of all deliverances, the teacher of all ways of deliverance. || 13 ||
The Chanting of the Names of Mañjuśrī (Nāmasaṃgīti)
He has uprooted existence with its twelve links, he maintains the purity of the twelve aspects;
he possesses the form of the method of the four truths and maintains the realization of the eight knowledges.

He who knows the meaning of the Truth through twelve aspects, who knows Reality through sixteen aspects, and whose perfect awakening consists of twenty aspects—he is the Fully Awakened One, the supreme all-knower. (15)
He manifests ten million emanation bodies of the Śrāvakas and Buddhas;
he is the realization of all moments of existence and the one who has transcended all states of mind. 16.
He manifests the vision of the world through various names, methods, and means;
having emerged from the three vehicles, he abides in the fruit of the single vehicle. || 17 ||

His self is purified of the realm of afflictions; he brings about the exhaustion of the realm of karma. Having crossed over the ocean of the floods, he has emerged from the mire of worldly yoga. || 18 ||
Having utterly abandoned the afflictions, secondary afflictions, and defilements, he is free from fear;
through wisdom as his vehicle and great compassion, he accomplishes the welfare of the world unfailingly. (13)
Pārtha has abandoned all conceptualizations; he is the object of consciousness and the one who brings about cessation.
He is the domain of the minds of all sentient beings and the movement of the minds of all sentient beings. || 20 ||
He has entered the minds of all sentient beings and attained equality with their thoughts;
he delights the minds of all and finds joy in the minds of all sentient beings.
Free from confusion regarding the final tenet, devoid of all delusion, possessing a mind that transcends doubt, he is the knower of all objects and consists of the three qualities. || 23 ||
He who discerns the five aggregates, the three times, and all moments;
he who is perfectly awakened in a single moment and upholds the essential nature of all Buddhas. (23)
He whose body is bodiless, who is worthy of being embodied, who manifests millions of bodies; he who perceives like the tip of a hair, the jewel-bannered one, the great gem.
The twenty-four [deities] beginning with Samatājñānagā.
The Chanting of the Names of Mañjuśrī (Nāmasaṃgīti)
He is that which is to be realized by all the perfectly awakened ones, the unsurpassed awakening of the Buddhas; he is the immediate source of mantra, the great mantra of the three families. || 1 ||
The generator of the meaning of all mantras, the great bindu, the syllable-less; the five-syllabled, the great emptiness, the bindu-emptiness, and the one beyond the six. (2)

He is devoid of all forms and yet possesses the formless; he bears the sixteenfold half-moon and the half-bindu. He is the digit who has transcended calculation, the possessor of the pinnacle of the fourth dhyāna.

He is the master of all the arts of meditative concentration, the knower of the lineage and clan of samādhis; he is the embodiment of the body of samādhi, the sovereign of all the bodies of enjoyment.

Clad in the saffron robe of the emanation body, he upholds the lineage of the Buddha’s emanations; manifesting throughout the ten directions as all-encompassing emanations, he acts for the sake of the world according to its needs.

He is the god beyond gods, the lord of the gods, the sovereign of the Suras, and the ruler of the Dānavas; he is the lord of the immortals, the preceptor of the gods, the one who destroys death, and the supreme lord among the Pramathas.
The Teacher, the Guru of the World, alone has crossed over the great abyss; he is the great lord of the gift of Dharma, renowned throughout the worlds of the ten directions. (7)
Girt with the armor of loving-kindness, clad in the mail of compassion, and armed with the sword, bow, and arrows of wisdom, he is the destroyer of afflictions and ignorance.
The enemy of Māra, the fearless hero, the destroyer of the fear of the four Māras, the leader of all Māra armies, the Perfectly Awakened One, the Guide of the World. || 3 ||
He is to be honored by forest-dwellers, worthy of worship, to be saluted, and always to be revered; he is most worthy of adoration, to be esteemed, to be bowed to, and the supreme teacher.

He whose stride traverses the three worlds, whose valor is boundless, who possesses the triple knowledge, who is learned in the Vedas, who is pure, who has the six superknowledges, and who possesses the sixfold recollections. || 11 ||
The Litany of Names (Nāmasaṃgīti)

The Bodhisattva Mahāsattva has transcended the world and possesses great supernatural power; he is established in the perfection of wisdom and has attained the state of one endowed with wisdom. || 12 ||
He is the knower of self and the knower of others, the All, the Most Excellent, the Son; having transcended all measurements, he is the supreme Lord of Knowledge, the one to be known. 13.

The Lord of the Gift of Dharma is supreme, the teacher of the fourfold great purpose; he is most worthy of being venerated by the worlds of those who proceed toward the three vehicles of deliverance. 14.
The great one, whose ear is pure in the ultimate sense, who is auspicious throughout the three worlds, the bringer of all prosperity, the glorious Mañjuśrī, the best among the illustrious. (15)
Fifteen verses on the knowledge of the performance of duties.
Homage to you, the Vajra who grants boons; homage be to you, the limit of all beings! Homage to you, whose essence is emptiness; homage be to you, the awakening of the Buddhas! (1)
O passion for the Buddha, homage be to you; O body of the Buddha, homage again and again. O joy of the Buddha, homage be to you; O delight of the Buddha, homage again and again. (2)
O Buddha-smile, homage to you; O Buddha-radiance, homage, homage! O Buddha-speech, may there be homage to you; O Buddha-nature, homage, homage! || 3 ||
O source of non-existence, homage be to you; homage to you, O source of the Buddha! O source of space, homage to you; homage to you, O source of primordial wisdom! || 4 ||
Homage to you, O Net of Illusion; homage to you, the Buddha’s drama! Homage to you who are all things for all; homage be to you, the Body of Gnosis. (5)
Thus end the five verses of praise for the wisdom of the five Tathāgatas.

O Vajrapāṇi, O Vajradhara, this is the Peerless Purity of Names, the *Nāmasaṃgīti*—the hymn of praise for Mañjuśrī-jñānasattva, the Wisdom-Body of all Tathāgatas, the Wisdom-Form of the Blessed One—for the sake of generating supreme joy, serene faith, and great delight within body and speech.
The *Nāmasaṃgīti*.
For the sake of the complete fulfillment and purification of the immeasurable accumulations of merit and wisdom on the perfectly full and pure stages;
for the attainment of the unsurpassed goal not yet attained; and for the realization of that which has not been reached.

"O Vajrapāṇi, as long as the eye of the Dharma of the entire assembly of Tathāgatas is maintained, it has been taught, revealed, explained, analyzed, clarified, and empowered by me within that mental continuum through the empowerment of the reality-nature (dharmatā) of all mantras.
This is the benefit of the first wheel; these are its eleven points.

Furthermore, Vāṇīvadha, this *Nāmasaṃgīti* is the body, speech, and mind of the utterly pure and purified omniscient gnosis; it is the awakening of all Tathāgatas and the realization of the perfectly enlightened Buddhas.
The movement of all Tathāgatas is in accordance with the realm of phenomena for their sons.
The defeat of all the forces of Māra belongs to the Victors.
The state of being endowed with the ten powers is [the perfection] of all those who possess the ten powers.
Omniscience is the source of all knowledges and of all the qualities of a Buddha.
The perfect realization of all Buddhas.
The complete fulfillment of the accumulations of merit and wisdom, which are stainless and perfectly pure, belongs to all the great bodhisattvas.
It is the source of all śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas.
It is the field for the excellence of all gods and humans.
It is the foundation of the Mahāyāna.
The arising of the conduct of a bodhisattva.
The culmination of the noble path.
It is the touchstone of the liberations and the source of the path of definitive emergence.
The lineage of the Tathāgatas is thus not subject to annihilation.
The increase of the family lineage of the great bodhisattvas.
The subjugation of all opposing disputants.
The destruction of all non-Buddhist teachers.
The defeat of the four Māras' army and host.
The gathering together of all sentient beings.
The maturation of the noble path belongs to those who encompass all modes of transcendence.
Concentration belongs to those who dwell in the four divine abodes.
Meditation is for those with one-pointed minds.
Yoga is the application of body, speech, and mind.
It is the dissociation from all fetters.
The abandonment of all defilements without exception.
The complete pacification of all obscurations.
Liberation from all bonds.
Liberation is the cessation of all obscurations.
It is the pacification of all disturbances of the mind.
A mine of all prosperities.
It is the abandonment of all misfortunes and the closing off of all states of woe.
Below this is the city of liberation.
The non-occurrence of the wheel of saṃsāra.
The setting in motion of the wheel of Dharma.
The parasols, banners, and streamers of the Tathāgata’s teaching have been raised high.
It is the basis for the teaching of all dharmas.
This is the established rule for those bodhisattvas who practice the conduct of the mantra-vehicle.
The attainment through cultivation belongs to those who are devoted to the perfection of wisdom.
The penetration of emptiness belongs to those devoted to meditative cultivation.
The penetration of the basis belongs to those devoted to inspired eloquence.
The Chanting of the Names (Nāmasaṃgīti)
The accomplishment of the entire equipment of the perfections.
Purification is for the sake of fulfilling the perfections of all the stages.
Penetration is the correct [realization] of the four noble truths.
The penetration of all phenomena into the single mind is the [fruit] of the four foundations of mindfulness.
This *Nāmasaṃgīti* [contains] all the qualities of the Buddhas until their complete perfection.
This is the benefit of the second wheel; its constituent parts are fifty-two.
Furthermore, Vajrapāṇi, O Vajradhara, this *Nāmasaṃgīti* pacifies the sins arising from the unwholesome conduct of body, speech, and mind of all sentient beings.
It is the purifier of all evil destinies for all sentient beings.
The Averter of All Evil Destinies.
It completely cuts through all karmic obscurations.
He brings about the non-arising of the non-arising of all eightfold conditions.
It brings about the pacification of the eight great fears.
The dispeller of all evil dreams.
She is the one who dispels all ill omens.
It brings about the pacification of all ill omens and obstacles.
It is that which removes all the activities of the enemy Māra.
It brings about the accumulation of all roots of merit and virtue.
It brings about the non-arising of all improper mental attention.
She is the one who utterly destroys the causes of all intoxication and pride.
It brings about the non-arising of all suffering and mental distress.
She is the heart-essence of all the Tathāgatas.
It is the secret of all bodhisattvas.
It is the secret of all śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas.
She has become the essence of all mudrās and mantras.
It brings about mindfulness and clear comprehension for those who proclaim that all phenomena are inexpressible.
It produces unsurpassed wisdom and intelligence; it brings about the perfection of health, strength, and sovereignty;
and it causes the increase of glory, auspiciousness, peace, and well-being.
It is that which brings forth glory, renown, fame, praise, and illumination.
It is that which brings about the pacification of all diseases and great fears.
Purified, the most purified among those who are purified.
The most purifying among the purifying.
The most blessed among the most blessed.
She is the most auspicious among all auspicious things.
A refuge for those seeking refuge.
A shelter for those seeking shelter.
A refuge for those seeking refuge.
The ultimate refuge for those who have no other refuge.
They are lamps for those who seek a lamp.
She has become the unsurpassed refuge for those who have no other resort.
They have become like vessels for those traveling to the further shore of the ocean of existence.
They have become like the great king of medicines by means of the eradication of all diseases.
Having become wisdom through the discernment of what is to be abandoned and what is to be adopted.
It has become the light of knowledge because it removes all the darkness of ignorance and false views.
They have become like wish-fulfilling gems because they fulfill the intentions and aspirations of all sentient beings according to their respective inclinations.
The Litany of Names, which is the omniscient wisdom of Mañjuśrī, the most auspicious of all that is most auspicious, for those seeking the supreme goal and the attainment of the [Buddha] body.
Having become one whose knowledge and vision are completely pure, for the sake of attaining the five eyes.
It consists in the complete fulfillment of the six perfections.
Likewise, the relinquishing of the gift of material goods, the gift of fearlessness, and the gift of the Dharma.

It has become the attainment of the ten stages through the fulfillment of the accumulations of merit and wisdom by means of the perfection of meditative concentration; it is free from the duality of phenomena because of its faith in the non-dual nature of reality.
Because it is free from the superimposition of other dharmas onto the nature of suchness.
It is because the limit of reality has the nature of the perfectly pure body of gnosis of the Tathāgata.
It is the state of emptiness in all its aspects, by virtue of its eradication of the dense thicket of all residual false views.
This *Nāmasaṃgīti* is the ineffable nature of all phenomena.
It is for the purpose of the dharma-nature of falling away, by means of the manifestation of the retention of the names.
This is the praise of the third wheel; its constituent phrases are fifty-two.

Furthermore, Vajrapāṇi, O Vajradhara, whatever son of good family or daughter of good family, practicing the conduct of the mantra-path, shall daily, at the three times, without interruption, preserve, recite, master, and properly attend to this *Nāmasaṃgīti*—the crest-jewel of names, the ultimate reality of the horse-headed one, the wisdom-body of the Blessed One Mañjuśrījñānasattva, the embodiment of the wisdom of all Tathāgatas—complete in its entirety, without deficiency, and without omission, using these very words and syllables.
And he will reveal it to others according to their capacity.
And focusing on each of the various meanings of those names one by one, having made the body of wisdom the object of focus, he will cultivate it with a one-pointed mind.

Abiding in a state of equanimity through the mental application of resolute faith and reality, and endowed with a supreme, unclouded wisdom that penetrates all phenomena and a corresponding faith, all the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas will gather together before that person who possesses the threefold purity and reveal to them the gateways of all dharmas.
And he will manifest his own physical form.

And the great wrathful kings who tame the haughty, such as Mahāvajradhara and others, who have become the protectors of the world, [bestow] vigor, strength, splendor, and invincibility through their various emanated bodies.
He will reveal the mandalas of the realization of all secret mantras.

Furthermore, the remaining mantra-kings of knowledge—the Great Pratyāṅgirā and the Great Parājitā, who are the subduers of all obstacles, Vināyakas, and Māras—will provide protection, defense, and concealment at every moment and in all activities throughout the day and night.
It will bestow the empowerment of all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas.
Through all [his] body, speech, and mind, he shall correctly empower his mental continuum.
And through the favor of all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas, they shall be graced with their assistance.
His eloquence will be the fearlessness regarding all phenomena, and he shall gather that as well.
It is selflessness through the disposition of love for the noble dharmas of all Arhats, Śrāvakas, and Pratyekabuddhas.
The Litany of Names.
And he will demonstrate existence as well.

And those such as Brahmā, Indra, Upendra, Rudra, Nārāyaṇa, Sanatkumāra, Maheśvara, Kārttikeya, Mahākāla, Nandikeśvara, Varuṇa, Kuvera, Hārītī, and the world-protectors of the ten directions—[they all] constantly and perpetually [attend] him whether he is walking or standing, lying down or sitting, sleeping or waking, composed or uncomposed, alone or in the midst of a great forest, or even in the midst of villages, towns, market-towns, hamlets, kingdoms, and royal capitals; whether he is in the middle of a crossroads, a carriage road, a city gate, a marketplace, a street, a square, or a place for drinking water, or even in an empty house, a mountain cave, a river valley, or a forest thicket.
Whether one is defiled by food remnants or free from them, intoxicated or heedless, it will at all times, in every way, and by every means provide supreme protection, defense, and guardianship.
Day and night, he will perform the supreme rite for well-being.

And whatever other gods, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kinnaras, mahoragas, humans, and non-humans there may be; and whatever others there are—the lords of the planets, constellations, and the hosts of mothers; and the seven Mothers; and the female birds, rākṣasīs, and piśācīs—all of them together, with their agreements, their armies, their retinues, and their followers, shall all provide protection, shelter, and guardianship.
And furthermore, he will obtain the power of silence within his body.
It will bestow health, strength, and an increase in lifespan.
This is the praise of the fourth wheel; its constituent phrases number nineteen.
Furthermore, Vajrapāṇi, O Vajradhara, whoever shall daily recite this *Nāmasaṃgīti*, the crest-jewel of names, three times with unbroken commitment, keeping it within their throat; |||
Or, reciting it from a book, he shall cause it to proceed.
Taking the Blessed One, the Mañjuśrī-jñānasattva, as his object of comparison, reflecting upon him and meditating upon his form.
In that very way, before long, by means of the Dharma and Vinaya, he will see all the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas situated in the expanse of the sky, together with their various emanated bodies.
That mahāsattva shall never, at any time, or in any way, fall into the miserable states or the lower realms.
Rebirth in a low family will not occur.
There is no rebirth in the borderlands or among the barbarians.
The Litany of Names.
It will come to pass.
He will not have deficient faculties.
He shall not have impaired faculties.
There will be no rebirth in a state characterized by wrong view.
He is not reborn in those Buddha-fields where no Buddhas have appeared.
There will be no state of being out of sight of the appearance of a Buddha and the Dharma taught by him.
And he is not reborn among the long-lived gods.
And one is not reborn during the intermediate aeons of the sword, characterized by famine, disease, and weapons.
And one is not reborn during the times of the five corruptions.
And there will be no fear of kings, enemies, or thieves.
And there is no fear of poverty resulting from every kind of deficiency.
And there shall be no fear of ill-repute, false accusation, censure, or infamy.
And he will be endowed with a noble birth, lineage, and clan among the people.
He will be endowed with a complexion that is supremely serene and exceedingly beautiful in color.
He will be dear and esteemed, pleasant to dwell with, and a joy to behold for the worlds.
O God, it will bring auspiciousness and good fortune to all beings.
Wherever he is reborn, in each and every birth, he will have a memory of his previous births.
He will possess great wealth and a great retinue; his wealth will be inexhaustible and his retinue inexhaustible.
He will become a refuge for all sentient beings, endowed with the qualities of the noble ones.
And he will be endowed with other immeasurable multitudes of qualities of this same kind.
And by nature, he will be endowed with the six immeasurable qualities.
And he will dwell in the four divine abodes.
He will be fully endowed with the powers of mindfulness, clear comprehension, and the knowledge of vows.
He will become an eloquent speaker, proficient in all the scriptures.
One will possess clear speech and a sharp, penetrating intellect.
He will become skillful, like fire, contented, a knower of the great goal, and free from craving.
And he will become one who inspires the highest confidence in all sentient beings.
And he comes to possess the virtues of the ācārya and the upādhyāya.
Furthermore, treatises on the crafts, arts, and sciences that he has never heard before will manifest to his intuition, both in their meaning and in their textual form.
And he will be one who conducts himself with the three modes of conduct characterized by perfectly pure ethical discipline.
He will have gone forth well and will be endowed with all perfections.
And he will possess the great mind of enlightenment, which is the non-forgetfulness of all-knowledge.
He shall never become one who has entered the fixed course of a śrāvaka, an arhat, or a pratyekabuddha.
This is the praise of the fifth wheel; its words are fifty-one.
The Chanting of the Names (Nāmasaṃgīti)
Thus, Vajrapāṇi, O Vajradhara, one who practices the conduct of the mantra-vehicle will be endowed with immeasurable qualities.
He will be endowed with other immeasurable qualities of this kind and of this nature.

Before long, Vajrapāṇi, the wielder of the vajra, the upholder of the *Paramārthanāmasaṃgīti*, a bull among men who has well accumulated the equipment of merit and wisdom, will swiftly perfect the qualities of a Buddha and realize unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment.

He is one whose nature is the inexhaustible, auspicious, and ultimate parinirvāṇa; he is the established Dharma King who teaches the unsurpassed Dharma to all sentient beings throughout the mandalas of the ten directions.
The benefits of the sixth wheel are immeasurable in their phrases.

*Śra śrā śraḥ*. All phenomena are pure by virtue of having non-existence as their intrinsic nature; all phenomena are primordially pure, because they partake in the purity of Mañjuśrī, the body of the gnosis of all Tathāgatas.
Śrāḥ! O heart of all Tathāgatas, take away, take away!

Śrīṃ Haṃ Hrīḥ! O Blessed One, embodiment of primordial wisdom, Lord of Speech, Great Voice, you whose essence is the wisdom of the dharmadhātu—immaculate and perfectly pure like the sky of all phenomena—Śrāḥ!
The Arrangement of Mantras.
The glorious Vajradhara, joyful and satisfied, bowed with palms joined to the Lord, the Perfectly Awakened One, the Blessed One, the Tathāgata. || 1 ||
Those words are fifty-one in number. From the perspective of their constituent parts.
O Vajrapāṇi, beginning with "O Vajradhara" and ending with "King of Armor"—these five benefits, taken together, constitute the *Nāmasaṃgīti*.
Together with many other lords of secrets, Vajrapāṇis, and kings of wrath, he spoke these words aloud: (2)
We rejoice, O Protector; excellent, excellent is this well-spoken word! You have performed for us a great service that brings about the attainment of perfect enlightenment. (3)
For this world, which is without a protector and yearns for the fruit of liberation, this pure path to the highest good has been proclaimed through the method of the *māyājāla*. (4)
Profound, vast, and extensive, of great significance and uncreated by the world—this is indeed the domain of the Buddhas, spoken by the Perfectly Enlightened One. (5)
Thus are the five concluding verses.

Thus concludes the *Paramārthanāmasaṃgīti* of the Blessed Mañjuśrījñānasattva, spoken by the Blessed Tathāgata Śākyamuni from the chapter on the Net of Samādhis within the *Āryamāyājāla*, the Great Yoga Tantra in sixteen thousand verses.

Śra śrā i ī u ū e ai mro yo yaḥ, you who abide in the heart as the embodiment of wisdom; O Buddha among Buddhas of the three times, oṃ vajratīkṣṇa, you who sever suffering, the embodiment of the wisdom of insight (prajñājñāna), the Lord of Speech of the Knowledge-Body (jñānakāya)—homage to you, the Architect!
May there be auspiciousness!
The Chanting of the Names of Mañjuśrī (Nāmasaṃgīti)

O Vajrapāṇi, wielder of the vajra, this is that peerless *Nāmasaṃgīti*—the hymn of praise for Mañjuśrī-jñānasattva, the embodiment of the wisdom of all Tathāgatas and the essence of the wisdom of the Blessed One—which produces incomparable joy, serene faith, and great exultation; which pacifies all diseases and the great terrors; and which is the most purifying of all purifiers.
O Vajrapāṇi, [you are] more blessed than the most blessed, the most auspicious of all auspicious things.
He is the refuge for those seeking refuge, the shelter for those seeking shelter, the protection for those seeking protection, and the final resort for those seeking a final resort.

They are lamps for those wanderers on earth who have no other resort; they are the unsurpassed goal for the Sugatas who have gone to the further shore of the ocean of existence; they are like the great king of medicines.
They have become like a sovereign wish-fulfilling gem for the mind, in order to dispel the blinding darkness of all false views.
She is the embodiment of omniscient wisdom for the sake of fulfilling the inclinations and intentions of all sentient beings regarding their states of woe.
They have attained the five eyes and have fulfilled the six perfections.

Furthermore, Vajrapāṇi, O Vajradhara, whoever shall take up this *Nāmasaṃgīti*, the crest-jewel, every day and recite it three times from memory, or read it from a book, shall cause it to proceed [in the world].
Furthermore, Vajrapāṇi, they will not be born into low families, nor will they have impaired faculties, nor will they be born with inferior faculties; rather, they are reborn in Buddha-fields.
And they are not reborn during eons of famine, disease, or weapons.
Furthermore, Vajrapāṇi, you shall be endowed with immeasurable qualities.
He will be endowed with immeasurable knowledge.
Furthermore, Vajrapāṇi, one who upholds, recites, reads aloud, and propagates this *Nāmasaṃgīti*—
Praise of the Benefits (Anuśaṃsāstuti)
